source.text: כִּֽי־יַכְרִ֞ית יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ אֶת־אַרְצָ֑ם וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֕ם וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֥ בְעָרֵיהֶ֖ם וּבְבָתֵּיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: When cuts off Yahweh your God the nations whose land Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, and you dispossess them and you dwell in their cities and in their houses,

en.L: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God cuts off the nations whose land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and live in their cities and in their houses,
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has destroyed the nations whose land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you, and you have driven them out and settled in their towns and houses,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will destroy the nations whose land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is giving you. You will drive them out and live in their towns and houses. When that time comes,

es.L: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios extermine las naciones cuya tierra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da, y tú las desposeas y habites en sus ciudades y en sus casas,
es.B: Cuando {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios haya destruido las naciones cuya tierra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da, y tú las hayas expulsado y te hayas establecido en sus ciudades y casas,
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios destruirá las naciones cuya tierra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te da. Tú las echarás y vivirás en sus ciudades y en sus casas. Cuando llegue ese momento,

fr.L: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu aura retranché les nations dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne le pays, et que tu les auras dépossédées et habiteras dans leurs villes et dans leurs maisons,
fr.B: Quand {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu aura détruit les nations dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne le pays, que tu les auras chassées et que tu te seras installé dans leurs villes et leurs maisons,
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu va détruire les nations dont {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne le pays. Tu vas les chasser et habiter dans leurs villes et leurs maisons. Quand ce moment sera venu,

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapoyakatilia mbali mataifa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa nchi yao, nawe ukayafukuza na kukaa katika miji yao na katika nyumba zao,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atakapokuwa ameyaangamiza mataifa ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa nchi yao, nawe ukiwa umeyafukuza na kuishi katika miji yao na nyumba zao,
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako atayaangamiza mataifa ambayo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anakupa nchi yao. Utayafukuza na kuishi katika miji yao na nyumba zao. Wakati huo utakapofika,

decisions.choice: the law of the cities of refuge, now for the land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The LORD commanded six cities of refuge, three on each side of the Jordan (Numbers 35:9-15). Moses has already set apart the three on the east side (4:41-43). This chapter commands the three in the land Israel is about to enter, and adds the rules that decide who may stay in them.

decisions.choice: cuts off: destroys, removes completely
decisions.reason: To "cut off" a nation is to destroy it as a people in its land. The same opening is used for the law on worship in 12:29.

decisions.choice: dispossess them: drive them out and take their place
decisions.reason: The verb means to take possession, and with people as its object, to take over what was theirs by driving them out. Israel will then live in the towns and houses the nations leave behind (6:10-11).

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both cities and smaller walled towns. Balanced and Readable say "towns" for ordinary places where people live, and keep "cities" in the fixed term "cities of refuge" (Readable "towns of safety", as Numbers 35). Literal says "cities" throughout.

decisions.choice: ... will destroy ... When that time comes,
decisions.reason: Readable states the events of the time clause as plain sentences, then picks up the time clause with "When that time comes", so that the command of verse 2 can follow in a short sentence. It says "he" for the second mention of the LORD.

decisions.choice: "tú" for Israel addressed in the singular ("tu Dios", "te"), with the plural_you span only where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verse 19, "you shall do to him")
decisions.reason: Moses addresses Israel as one person through the chapter, as the Hebrew singular forms show.

decisions.choice: "ciudades" at every level
decisions.reason: The English says "towns" at Balanced and Readable. Spanish keeps "ciudades", the word for the cities of refuge in Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 4, so that the towns of verse 1 and the cities set apart in verse 2 read as the same kind of place.

decisions.choice: "tu" for Israel addressed in the singular, "vous" where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verse 19)
decisions.reason: French follows the Hebrew number of "you", as in the rest of Deuteronomy.

decisions.choice: singular forms ("wako", "utayafukuza") for Israel addressed as one, plural ("mtamtendea") where the Hebrew turns to the plural (verse 19)
decisions.reason: Swahili follows the Hebrew number of "you", as in the rest of Deuteronomy.

source.text: שָׁל֥וֹשׁ עָרִ֖ים תַּבְדִּ֣יל לָ֑ךְ בְּת֣וֹךְ אַרְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: three cities you will set apart for yourself in [the] midst of your land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you to possess it.

en.L: you shall set apart three cities for yourself in the midst of your land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to take possession of [it].
en.B: you are to set apart three cities inside your land, the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to take as your own.
en.R: set apart three towns in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to own.

es.L: apartarás para ti tres ciudades en medio de tu tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da para que tomes posesión de [ella].
es.B: apartarás tres ciudades dentro de tu tierra, la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da para que la tomes como tuya.
es.R: aparta tres ciudades en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da para que sea tuya.

fr.L: tu mettras à part pour toi trois villes au milieu de ton pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour en prendre possession.
fr.B: tu réserveras trois villes à l’intérieur de ton pays, le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour qu’il soit à toi.
fr.R: mets à part trois villes dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour qu’il t’appartienne.

sw.L: utajitengea miji mitatu katikati ya nchi yako ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa uimiliki.
sw.B: utatenga miji mitatu ndani ya nchi yako, nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa iwe yako.
sw.R: tenga miji mitatu katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa iwe mali yako.

decisions.choice: set apart: separate for a special purpose
decisions.reason: The verb means to divide one thing from others. It is used of Moses setting apart the three eastern cities (4:41) and of the Levites set apart for the LORD's service (10:8).

decisions.choice: in the midst of your land: within the land west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: "Your land" here is the land Israel will take after crossing the river, as verse 1 describes. The three cities east of the Jordan are already set apart (4:41-43).

decisions.choice: for yourself: for the people's own use
decisions.reason: Moses speaks to Israel as one person, "you". The cities are for the whole people, to protect any of them who kills by accident. The word has its pausal form here, at a pause in the verse; the sense is the same as elsewhere.

decisions.choice: to own
decisions.reason: Readable says "to own" for "to possess it", in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep "to possess".

source.text: תָּכִ֣ין לְךָ֮ הַדֶּרֶךְ֒ וְשִׁלַּשְׁתָּ֙ אֶת־גְּב֣וּל אַרְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַנְחִֽילְךָ֖ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְהָיָ֕ה לָנ֥וּס שָׁ֖מָּה כָּל־רֹצֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: You will prepare for yourself the road, and you will divide into three [the] territory of your land which will give you as inheritance Yahweh your God, and it will be for fleeing there [for] every killer.

en.L: You shall prepare the road for yourself, and divide into three [parts] the territory of your land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God gives you as an inheritance; and it shall be for every killer to flee there.
en.B: Prepare the roads, and divide into three regions the territory {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as your inheritance. Then anyone who has killed someone can flee to one of these cities.
en.R: Make the roads to these towns ready. Divide the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you into three parts, with one town in each part. Then anyone who has killed a person can run away to one of them.

es.L: Prepararás para ti el camino, y dividirás en tres [partes] el territorio de tu tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da en herencia; y será para que huya allí todo homicida.
es.B: Prepara los caminos, y divide en tres regiones el territorio que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da como herencia. Así, cualquiera que haya matado a alguien podrá huir a una de esas ciudades.
es.R: Prepara los caminos que llevan a esas ciudades. Divide en tres partes la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da, con una ciudad en cada parte. Así, quien haya matado a alguien podrá huir a una de ellas.

fr.L: Tu prépareras pour toi la route, et tu diviseras en trois [parties] le territoire de ton pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne en héritage ; et ce sera pour que tout meurtrier puisse s’y enfuir.
fr.B: Prépare les routes, et divise en trois régions le territoire que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne en héritage. Ainsi, quiconque a tué quelqu’un pourra s’enfuir dans l’une de ces villes.
fr.R: Prépare les routes qui mènent à ces villes. Divise en trois parties le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne, avec une ville dans chaque partie. Ainsi, celui qui a tué quelqu’un pourra s’enfuir dans l’une d’elles.

sw.L: Utajitengenezea njia, na kuligawa katika [sehemu] tatu eneo la nchi yako ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa kuwa urithi; nayo itakuwa ili kila mwuaji akimbilie huko.
sw.B: Tengeneza njia, na uligawe katika maeneo matatu eneo ambalo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa kuwa urithi wako. Hivyo mtu yeyote aliyeua mtu ataweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hiyo.
sw.R: Tengeneza njia za kwenda kwenye miji hiyo. Igawe nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa katika sehemu tatu, kila sehemu ikiwa na mji mmoja. Hivyo mtu aliyeua mtu ataweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hiyo.

decisions.choice: prepare the road: make the way to the cities ready and easy to travel
alternatives: measure the distances to the cities
decisions.reason: The verb means to make ready or to set firmly in place. With "the road" it most likely means to keep the roads to the cities open and in good order, so that a killer can reach one quickly (verse 6). Some read it as "measure the way", that is, work out the distances so that the three cities are evenly placed, which would fit the dividing of the land in the next clause.

decisions.choice: divide into three: three districts, one city in each
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the number three. The land is to be divided into three regions, each with its own city, so that no part of it is too far from a refuge (verse 6). Joshua 20:7 names one city in the north, one in the middle and one in the south.

decisions.choice: every killer: anyone who has taken a human life
decisions.reason: The word names anyone who has killed a person, whether by accident or on purpose (Numbers 35:6). Anyone may flee to the city; verses 4-13 then decide who may stay there and who must be handed over.

decisions.choice: anyone who has killed someone
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "killer" for this word every time, as in Numbers 35. Balanced and Readable say "anyone who has killed someone" where the killing may have been an accident, and "murderer" where the law speaks of a deliberate killing (verses 11-12).

decisions.choice: the roads / to these towns; with one town in each part
decisions.reason: Balanced says "roads", since the road to each city is meant. Readable adds "to these towns" and "with one town in each part", which the purpose of the dividing implies (verses 2 and 6).

decisions.choice: "le meurtrier" (L), "celui qui a tué quelqu'un" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one word for the Hebrew "killer", as in Deuteronomy 4:42 and Numbers 35, taken in its older sense of anyone who has caused a death. Balanced and Readable say "celui qui a tué quelqu'un" where the killing may be an accident, and keep "meurtrier" for deliberate killing (verse 12).

source.text: וְזֶה֙ דְּבַ֣ר הָרֹצֵ֔חַ אֲשֶׁר־יָנ֥וּס שָׁ֖מָּה וָחָ֑י אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַכֶּ֤ה אֶת־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ בִּבְלִי־דַ֔עַת וְה֛וּא לֹא־שֹׂנֵ֥א ל֖וֹ מִתְּמֹ֥ל שִׁלְשֹֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is the] case of the killer who will flee there and live: who strikes his neighbor without knowledge, and he not [was] hating him from yesterday [and the] third day.

en.L: And this [is] the case of the killer who may flee there and live: whoever strikes his neighbor without knowing, and he was not hating him in time past.
en.B: This is the rule for the killer who may flee there and stay alive: it is anyone who kills a neighbor by accident, without having hated that neighbor before.
en.R: Here is who may run to one of these towns and stay alive. It is someone who killed another person by accident, and who had not hated that person before.

es.L: Y este [es] el caso del homicida que podrá huir allí y vivir: el que hiera a su prójimo sin saber[lo], no habiéndolo odiado en tiempo pasado.
es.B: Esta es la norma para quien haya matado a alguien y pueda huir allí y salvar la vida: es cualquiera que mate a su prójimo por accidente, sin haberlo odiado antes.
es.R: Esta es la persona que puede huir a una de esas ciudades y salvar su vida. Es quien mató a otra persona por accidente y no la odiaba antes.

fr.L: Et voici le cas du meurtrier qui pourra s’enfuir là et vivre : celui qui aura frappé son prochain sans le savoir, et qui ne le haïssait pas auparavant.
fr.B: Voici la règle pour celui qui a tué et qui peut s’enfuir là pour rester en vie : il s’agit de quiconque a tué son prochain par accident, sans l’avoir haï auparavant.
fr.R: Voici qui peut s’enfuir dans l’une de ces villes et rester en vie. C’est celui qui a tué une autre personne par accident, et qui ne la détestait pas avant.

sw.L: Na hii [ndiyo] habari ya mwuaji atakayekimbilia huko na kuishi: yeyote ampigaye jirani yake bila kujua, wala hakuwa akimchukia tangu zamani.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo hali ya mtu aliyeua ambaye anaweza kukimbilia huko na kubaki hai: ni mtu yeyote anayemwua jirani yake kwa bahati mbaya, bila kuwa amemchukia hapo kabla.
sw.R: Huyu ndiye mtu anayeweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hii na kubaki hai. Ni mtu aliyemwua mwenzake kwa bahati mbaya, na ambaye hakuwa amemchukia hapo kabla.

decisions.choice: the case: the rule that applies
decisions.reason: The word means a word or a matter. Here it introduces the kind of killer the law protects, as in 15:2 it introduces the rule for the release of debts.

decisions.choice: strikes ... without knowledge: kills without meaning to
decisions.reason: To strike someone here is to deal a blow that kills. "Without knowledge" means without intending it, by accident, as in 4:42. Verse 5 gives an example.

decisions.choice: from yesterday and the third day: before, in time past
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "yesterday and the day before" for any time before. The killer had no hatred for the one who died, which shows that it was not murder (4:42; verse 11).

decisions.choice: his neighbor: a fellow member of the community
decisions.reason: The word means a companion or fellow, anyone a person lives and works with, not only someone living next door. The law is written with masculine words but covers any killer and any victim (4:42).

decisions.choice: anyone who kills a neighbor ... that neighbor / another person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive, as in 4:42. Literal keeps the masculine words of the Hebrew.

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁר֩ יָבֹ֨א אֶת־רֵעֵ֥הוּ בַיַּעַר֮ לַחְטֹ֣ב עֵצִים֒ וְנִדְּחָ֨ה יָד֤וֹ בַגַּרְזֶן֙ לִכְרֹ֣ת הָעֵ֔ץ וְנָשַׁ֤ל הַבַּרְזֶל֙ מִן־הָעֵ֔ץ וּמָצָ֥א אֶת־רֵעֵ֖הוּ וָמֵ֑ת ה֗וּא יָנ֛וּס אֶל־אַחַ֥ת הֶעָרִים־הָאֵ֖לֶּה וָחָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And who goes with his neighbor into the forest to cut wood, and is driven his hand with the axe to cut down the tree, and slips the iron from the wood and finds his neighbor and he dies, he will flee to one of the cities these and live;

en.L: As when one goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and his hand swings with the ax to cut down the tree, and the iron slips off the wood and finds his neighbor, and he dies: he shall flee to one of these cities and live,
en.B: For example, someone goes into the forest with a neighbor to cut wood. As the ax is swung to fell a tree, the head flies off the handle and strikes the neighbor, who dies. The one who was cutting may flee to one of these cities and stay alive,
en.R: Suppose two neighbors go into the woods to cut wood. One of them swings an ax to chop down a tree, but the ax head comes off the handle. It hits the other one, who dies. The one who swung the ax can run away to one of these towns and stay alive.

es.L: Como cuando alguien entra en el bosque con su prójimo a cortar leña, y su mano empuja el hacha para cortar el árbol, y el hierro se suelta de la madera y alcanza a su prójimo, y este muere: él huirá a una de estas ciudades y vivirá,
es.B: Por ejemplo, alguien va al bosque con su prójimo a cortar leña. Al blandir el hacha para derribar un árbol, la cabeza se sale del mango y golpea al compañero, que muere. El que estaba cortando podrá huir a una de estas ciudades y salvar la vida,
es.R: Supongamos que dos vecinos van al bosque a cortar leña. Uno de ellos da un golpe con el hacha para tumbar un árbol, pero la cabeza del hacha se sale del mango. Golpea al otro, y este muere. El que movió el hacha puede huir a una de estas ciudades y salvar su vida.

fr.L: Ainsi, quand quelqu’un va dans la forêt avec son prochain pour couper du bois, que sa main s’élance avec la hache pour abattre l’arbre, que le fer se détache du bois et atteigne son prochain, et qu’il meure : celui-là s’enfuira dans l’une de ces villes et vivra,
fr.B: Par exemple, quelqu’un va dans la forêt avec son prochain pour couper du bois. Au moment où il lève la hache pour abattre un arbre, le fer se détache du manche et frappe son compagnon, qui meurt. Celui qui coupait le bois pourra s’enfuir dans l’une de ces villes et rester en vie,
fr.R: Imaginons que deux voisins aillent couper du bois dans la forêt. L’un d’eux donne un coup de hache pour abattre un arbre, mais le fer se détache du manche. Il frappe l’autre, qui meurt. Celui qui tenait la hache peut s’enfuir dans l’une de ces villes et rester en vie.

sw.L: Kama mtu aendapo msituni pamoja na jirani yake kukata kuni, na mkono wake ukapiga kwa shoka ili kuukata mti, na chuma kikachomoka kutoka kwenye mti, kikampata jirani yake, naye akafa: yeye atakimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hii na kuishi,
sw.B: Kwa mfano, mtu anakwenda msituni pamoja na jirani yake kukata kuni. Anapopiga shoka ili kuangusha mti, kichwa cha shoka kinachomoka kwenye mpini na kumpiga jirani yake, naye akafa. Yule aliyekuwa akikata anaweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hii na kubaki hai,
sw.R: Tuseme majirani wawili wanakwenda porini kukata kuni. Mmoja wao anapiga shoka ili kuangusha mti, lakini kichwa cha shoka kinachomoka kwenye mpini. Kinampiga yule mwingine, naye anakufa. Yule aliyepiga shoka anaweza kukimbilia mmojawapo wa miji hii na kubaki hai.

decisions.choice: and one who: an example of a killing without knowledge
decisions.reason: The verse gives a case that fits the rule of verse 4: two people at work together, and a death no one intended.

decisions.choice: his hand is driven with the ax: he swings the ax hard
decisions.reason: The verb means to be pushed or driven. The picture is of the full swing of the arm as the ax comes down on the tree.

decisions.choice: the iron slips from the wood: the ax head comes off its wooden handle
alternatives: the iron glances off the tree
decisions.reason: "The iron" is the head of the ax, and "the wood" most likely its handle. The same word was just used for the tree being cut, so the words could also mean that the iron glances off the tree, or that a chip flies from it, but the head flying off the handle is the plainest sense.

decisions.choice: finds his neighbor: hits him
decisions.reason: To "find" here is to reach or strike, as an arrow or a blow finds its mark. It stresses that the blow was not aimed at him.

decisions.choice: the head ... the handle
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the parts of the ax, so the picture is clear. Literal keeps "the iron" and "the wood". Balanced and Literal end the verse with a comma, since verse 6 gives the reason for the rule.

source.text: פֶּן־יִרְדֹּף֩ גֹּאֵ֨ל הַדָּ֜ם אַחֲרֵ֣י הָרֹצֵ֗חַ כִּי־יֵחַם֮ לְבָבוֹ֒ וְהִשִּׂיג֛וֹ כִּֽי־יִרְבֶּ֥ה הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ וְהִכָּ֣הוּ נָ֑פֶשׁ וְלוֹ֙ אֵ֣ין מִשְׁפַּט־מָ֔וֶת כִּ֠י לֹ֣א שֹׂנֵ֥א ה֛וּא ל֖וֹ מִתְּמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: lest pursue the avenger of the blood after the killer, for is hot his heart, and overtake him, for is long the way, and strike him [as to] life; and to him not [is a] sentence of death, for not hating he [was] him from yesterday [and the] third day.

en.L: lest the avenger of blood pursue the killer while his heart is hot, and overtake him because the way is long, and strike him dead; and for him [there is] no sentence of death, since he was not hating him in time past.
en.B: or else the avenger of blood, in the heat of anger, might chase the killer, catch up because the way is long, and kill {{gender:them|him}}. Yet that person did not deserve to die, having had no hatred for the dead neighbor before.
en.R: If the town is too far away, the relative who avenges the death might chase the killer in a rage, catch up and kill {{gender:them|him}}. But the killer did not deserve to die, because the killer had not hated the person who died.

es.L: no sea que el vengador de la sangre persiga al homicida mientras su corazón está enardecido, y lo alcance porque el camino es largo, y lo hiera de muerte; y no [hay] para él sentencia de muerte, pues no lo odiaba en tiempo pasado.
es.B: de lo contrario, el vengador de la sangre, en el ardor de su ira, podría perseguir al que mató, alcanzarlo porque el camino es largo y matarlo. Sin embargo, esa persona no merecía morir, pues antes no tenía ningún odio contra el prójimo que murió.
es.R: Si la ciudad está demasiado lejos, el pariente que venga la muerte podría perseguir con furia al que mató, alcanzarlo y matarlo. Pero el que mató no merecía morir, porque no odiaba a la persona que murió.

fr.L: de peur que le vengeur du sang ne poursuive le meurtrier tandis que son cœur est échauffé, ne l’atteigne parce que le chemin est long, et ne le frappe à mort ; or il n’y a pas pour lui de sentence de mort, puisqu’il ne le haïssait pas auparavant.
fr.B: sinon le vengeur du sang, dans le feu de la colère, pourrait poursuivre celui qui a tué, le rattraper parce que le chemin est long, et le tuer. Pourtant cette personne ne méritait pas la mort, puisqu’elle n’avait aucune haine auparavant pour le prochain qui est mort.
fr.R: Si la ville est trop loin, le parent qui venge le mort pourrait poursuivre dans sa colère celui qui a tué, le rattraper et le tuer. Mais celui qui a tué ne méritait pas de mourir, car il ne détestait pas la personne qui est morte.

sw.L: mlipiza kisasi wa damu asije akamfuatia mwuaji moyo wake ukiwa na hasira kali, akampata kwa sababu njia ni ndefu, akampiga hata akafa; wala kwake hakuna hukumu ya kifo, kwa kuwa hakuwa akimchukia tangu zamani.
sw.B: la sivyo mlipiza kisasi wa damu, akiwa amewaka hasira, angeweza kumfuatia mtu aliyeua, kumpata kwa sababu njia ni ndefu, na kumwua. Lakini mtu huyo hakustahili kufa, kwa kuwa hakuwa na chuki dhidi ya jirani aliyekufa hapo kabla.
sw.R: Ikiwa mji uko mbali sana, ndugu anayelipiza kisasi angeweza kumfuatia kwa hasira mtu aliyeua, akampata na kumwua. Lakini mtu aliyeua hakustahili kufa, kwa sababu hakuwa amemchukia yule aliyekufa.

decisions.choice: the avenger of blood: the dead person's near relative, who was to take life for life
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the relative who stands up for the family and buys back its land (Leviticus 25:25). When one of the family was killed, this relative was bound to pursue the killer (Numbers 35:12, 19).

decisions.choice: his heart is hot: in the heat of anger
decisions.reason: A "hot heart" is rage. The relative's anger would not wait to ask whether the killing was an accident.

decisions.choice: because the way is long: the reason for verses 2-3
decisions.reason: If the city is far off, the killer may be caught before reaching it. This is why the land is divided into three and the roads made ready.

decisions.choice: strike him in life: kill him
decisions.reason: To strike someone "as to the life" is to deal a deadly blow (verse 11; Genesis 37:21).

decisions.choice: for him there is no sentence of death: he does not deserve to die
decisions.reason: The killing was not murder, so the law does not condemn the killer to death. If the avenger killed him, an innocent life would be taken (verse 10).

decisions.choice: If the town is too far away
decisions.reason: Readable puts "because the way is long" first, as a plain condition, so the reason for the rule is clear.

decisions.choice: them / him
decisions.reason: The killer may be a man or a woman, so Balanced and Readable use the gender setting for the pronoun. Readable repeats "the killer" rather than use a pronoun with a verb that would change with the setting.

decisions.choice: "alcanzarlo ... matarlo", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English has a gender setting for "them|him", the Spanish pronoun refers back to "el que mató", which already means anyone who killed; generic "lo" needs no alternative wording. The same holds in verses 12-13.

decisions.choice: "le rattraper ... le tuer", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Where the English has a gender setting for "them|him", the French pronoun refers back to "celui qui a tué", which already means anyone who killed; generic "le" needs no alternative wording. The same holds in verses 12-13.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֛ן אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר שָׁלֹ֥שׁ עָרִ֖ים תַּבְדִּ֥יל לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I [am] commanding you, saying, three cities you will set apart for yourself.

en.L: Therefore I am commanding you, saying, 'You shall set apart three cities for yourself.'
en.B: That is why I command you to set apart three cities.
en.R: That is why I am telling you to set apart three towns.

es.L: Por eso yo te mando, diciendo: “Apartarás para ti tres ciudades”.
es.B: Por eso te ordeno que apartes tres ciudades.
es.R: Por eso te digo que apartes tres ciudades.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je te commande, en disant : “Tu mettras à part pour toi trois villes.”
fr.B: Voilà pourquoi je t’ordonne de mettre à part trois villes.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que je te dis de mettre à part trois villes.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo ninakuamuru, nikisema, 'Utajitengea miji mitatu.'
sw.B: Ndiyo maana ninakuamuru kutenga miji mitatu.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu ninakuambia utenge miji mitatu.

decisions.choice: therefore: the command of verse 2, now with its reason
decisions.reason: Having explained why the cities are needed (verses 4-6), Moses repeats the command of verse 2 in the same words.

decisions.choice: '...' at Literal; no quotation at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "saying" and sets the command in single quotation marks, since it is quoted within Moses' speech. Balanced and Readable give it as a plain instruction.

source.text: וְאִם־יַרְחִ֞יב יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת־גְּבֻ֣לְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וְנָ֤תַן לְךָ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לָתֵ֥ת לַאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if enlarges Yahweh your God your territory, just as he swore to your fathers, and gives to you all the land which he spoke to give to your fathers,

en.L: And if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God enlarges your territory, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers, and gives you all the land that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke of giving to your fathers,
en.B: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God extends your borders, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} on oath, and gives you all the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give them,
en.R: Someday {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God may make your land larger, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}. He may give you all the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised them.

es.L: Y si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios ensancha tu territorio, como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} juró a tus padres, y te da toda la tierra que habló de dar a tus padres,
es.B: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios extiende tus fronteras, como lo prometió con juramento a tus antepasados, y te da toda la tierra que dijo que les daría,
es.R: Algún día {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios podría hacer más grande tu tierra, como se lo juró a tus antepasados. Podría darte toda la tierra que les prometió.

fr.L: Et si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu élargit ton territoire, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a juré à tes pères, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne tout le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit donner à tes pères,
fr.B: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu étend tes frontières, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a promis par serment à tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}, et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te donne tout le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur donnerait,
fr.R: Un jour, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu agrandira peut-être ton pays, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a juré à tes {{gender:ancêtres|pères}}. Il pourra te donner tout le pays qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a promis.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako akipanua eneo lako, kama alivyowaapia baba zako, akakupa nchi yote aliyosema kwamba atawapa baba zako,
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako akipanua mipaka yako, kama alivyowaahidi mababu zako kwa kiapo, na kukupa nchi yote aliyosema angewapa,
sw.R: Siku moja {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako huenda akaipanua nchi yako, kama alivyowaapia mababu zako. Huenda akakupa nchi yote aliyowaahidi.

decisions.choice: enlarges your territory, as he swore: the promise of the whole land
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham's descendants land as far as the Euphrates (Genesis 15:18; Deuteronomy 1:7-8; 11:24). Israel will not hold all of it at first (7:22); 12:20 also speaks of the time when the LORD enlarges the land.

decisions.choice: if: a future that depends on what follows
decisions.reason: The verse looks beyond the first settlement. Verse 9 says on what it depends and what Israel is to do then.

decisions.choice: he spoke: he promised
decisions.reason: "Spoke to give" means said that he would give, a promise (6:3; 9:28).

decisions.choice: promised / said he would give; ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "promised" or "said he would" for "spoke", and "ancestors" through the gender setting, as in 1:11. Readable adds "Someday" to show the future in view, and starts a new sentence with "He".

source.text: כִּֽי־תִשְׁמֹר֩ אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֨ה הַזֹּ֜את לַעֲשֹׂתָ֗הּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֣י מְצַוְּךָ֮ הַיּוֹם֒ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ וְלָלֶ֥כֶת בִּדְרָכָ֖יו כָּל־הַיָּמִ֑ים וְיָסַפְתָּ֨לְךָ֥ עוֹד֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ עָרִ֔ים עַ֖ל הַשָּׁלֹ֥שׁ הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: because you keep all the commandment this to do it, which I [am] commanding you today, to love Yahweh your God and to walk in his ways all the days, and you add for yourself again three cities to the three these,

en.L: because you keep all this commandment, to do it, which I am commanding you today, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways all the days, then you shall add three more cities for yourself to these three,
en.B: because you are careful to keep this whole commandment that I give you today, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and to walk always in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, then add three more cities to these three,
en.R: This will happen if you obey all the commands I am giving you today, loving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and always living the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does this, set apart three more towns besides these three.

es.L: porque guardas todo este mandamiento para cumplirlo, el cual yo te mando hoy, de amar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios y andar en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos todos los días, entonces añadirás para ti tres ciudades más a estas tres,
es.B: porque tienes cuidado de guardar todo este mandamiento que te doy hoy, de amar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios y andar siempre en {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} caminos, entonces añade tres ciudades más a estas tres,
es.R: Esto sucederá si obedeces todos los mandamientos que te doy hoy, amando {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios y viviendo siempre como {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiere. Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo haga, aparta tres ciudades más, además de estas tres.

fr.L: parce que tu gardes tout ce commandement pour le pratiquer, [celui] que je te commande aujourd’hui, d’aimer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et de marcher dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} voies tous les jours, alors tu ajouteras pour toi encore trois villes à ces trois-là,
fr.B: parce que tu veilles à garder tout ce commandement que je te donne aujourd’hui, à aimer {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et à marcher toujours dans {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} voies, alors ajoute trois autres villes à ces trois-là,
fr.R: Cela arrivera si tu obéis à tous les commandements que je te donne aujourd’hui, en aimant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu et en vivant toujours comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le veut. Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’aura fait, mets à part trois autres villes en plus de ces trois-là.

sw.L: kwa sababu unaishika amri hii yote kuitenda, ninayokuamuru leo, kumpenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na kuenenda katika njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} siku zote, basi utajiongezea miji mitatu mingine juu ya hii mitatu,
sw.B: kwa sababu unaishika kwa uangalifu amri hii yote ninayokupa leo, ya kumpenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na kuenenda daima katika njia {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, basi ongeza miji mitatu mingine juu ya hii mitatu,
sw.R: Hili litatokea ukizitii amri zote ninazokupa leo, ukimpenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako na kuishi daima jinsi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anavyotaka. Atakapofanya hivyo, tenga miji mitatu mingine zaidi ya hii mitatu.

decisions.choice: because: the enlarging of the land depends on Israel's faithfulness
decisions.reason: The word can mean "because" or "when, provided that". Either way, the gift of the whole land is tied to Israel's keeping the commandment, as in 11:22-24.

decisions.choice: all this commandment: the whole of Moses' teaching taken as one
decisions.reason: The singular "commandment" stands for everything Moses commands, summed up as loving the LORD and walking in his ways (6:1, 25; 11:22).

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as he directs
decisions.reason: To walk in someone's ways is to follow his way of life. "All the days" means always (8:6; 10:12).

decisions.choice: three more cities: a further three if the land grows
decisions.reason: The added cities would serve the larger land, so that every part stays within reach of a refuge. Scripture does not record that these three further cities were ever set apart.

decisions.choice: This will happen if ...; When he does this
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link between the promise of verse 8 and the condition of this verse explicit in two short sentences.

source.text: וְלֹ֤א יִשָּׁפֵךְ֙ דָּ֣ם נָקִ֔י בְּקֶ֣רֶב אַרְצְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ נַחֲלָ֑ה וְהָיָ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ דָּמִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and not will be shed innocent blood in [the] midst of your land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you [as] an inheritance, and will be on you bloods.

en.L: so that innocent blood may not be shed in the midst of your land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you [as] an inheritance, and bloodguilt be on you.
en.B: so that innocent blood is not shed in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you do not become guilty of bloodshed.
en.R: This will keep innocent people from being killed in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as your own. If that happened, you would be guilty of their death.

es.L: para que no se derrame sangre inocente en medio de tu tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da [como] herencia, ni haya sobre ti culpa de sangre.
es.B: para que no se derrame sangre inocente en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da como herencia, y no te hagas culpable de derramar sangre.
es.R: Así no se matará a gente inocente en la tierra que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios te da como tuya. Si eso pasara, tú serías culpable de su muerte.

fr.L: afin que le sang innocent ne soit pas répandu au milieu de ton pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne [en] héritage, et que [la culpabilité du] sang ne soit pas sur toi.
fr.B: afin que le sang innocent ne soit pas versé dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne en héritage, et que tu ne deviennes pas coupable d’avoir versé le sang.
fr.R: Ainsi, des innocents ne seront pas tués dans le pays que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu te donne pour qu’il t’appartienne. Si cela arrivait, tu serais coupable de leur mort.

sw.L: ili damu isiyo na hatia isimwagwe katikati ya nchi yako ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa [kuwa] urithi, wala hatia ya damu isiwe juu yako.
sw.B: ili damu isiyo na hatia isimwagike katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa kuwa urithi, nawe usiwe na hatia ya kumwaga damu.
sw.R: Hivyo watu wasio na hatia hawatauawa katika nchi ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako anakupa iwe yako. Hilo likitokea, wewe ungekuwa na hatia ya vifo vyao.

decisions.choice: innocent blood: the life of someone who does not deserve death
decisions.reason: Here it is the life of the accidental killer, if the avenger caught him before he reached safety (verse 6).

decisions.choice: bloods: guilt for bloodshed
decisions.reason: The plural of "blood" means the guilt that comes from taking a life wrongly (Exodus 22:1; Numbers 35:33).

decisions.choice: and blood be on you: what would follow if innocent blood were shed
decisions.reason: The second clause states the result the cities prevent. If the people failed to provide refuge, the guilt of the death would rest on them all, as on a town near which a body is found (21:1-9).

decisions.choice: If that happened, you would be guilty of their death.
decisions.reason: Readable states the result in a sentence of its own. Balanced says "you do not become guilty", which carries the "not" of the first clause into the second.

source.text: וְכִֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה אִישׁ֙ שֹׂנֵ֣א לְרֵעֵ֔הוּ וְאָ֤רַב לוֹ֙ וְקָ֣ם עָלָ֔יו וְהִכָּ֥הוּ נֶ֖פֶשׁ וָמֵ֑ת וְנָ֕ס אֶל־אַחַ֖ת הֶעָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: But if there is a man hating his neighbor, and he lies in wait for him and rises against him and strikes him [as to] life and he dies, and he flees to one of the cities these,

en.L: But if there is a man hating his neighbor, and he lies in wait for him and rises up against him and strikes him dead, and he dies, and he flees to one of these cities,
en.B: But if someone hates a neighbor, lies in wait, attacks and kills that neighbor, and then flees to one of these cities,
en.R: But suppose someone who hates another person hides and waits, then attacks and kills that person, and then runs away to one of these towns.

decisions.choice: hating: hostile beforehand
decisions.reason: This is the opposite of the case in verses 4 and 6, where the killer "was not hating him in time past". Hatred held before the act shows that the killing was meant.

decisions.choice: lies in wait and rises against him: a planned attack
decisions.reason: To lie in wait is to watch for someone in order to attack; to rise against him is to set upon him. Both show intent, as in Numbers 35:20 and Exodus 21:13-14.

decisions.choice: strikes him as to life: kills him
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone
decisions.reason: The law uses "a man" for anyone who does this, as Hebrew laws usually do (4:42).

decisions.choice: someone ... that neighbor / that person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use inclusive words and repeat the noun rather than use pronouns. Literal keeps the masculine words of the Hebrew.

source.text: וְשָֽׁלְחוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י עִיר֔וֹ וְלָקְח֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ מִשָּׁ֑ם וְנָתְנ֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ בְּיַ֛ד גֹּאֵ֥ל הַדָּ֖ם וָמֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: then will send [the] elders of his city and take him from there and give him into [the] hand of [the] avenger of the blood, and he will die.

en.L: then the elders of his city shall send and take him from there and give him into the hand of the avenger of blood, and he shall die.
en.B: the elders of the murderer's own town are to send for {{gender:them|him}}, bring {{gender:them|him}} back from there and hand {{gender:them|him}} over to the avenger of blood to be put to death.
en.R: The elders of the murderer's hometown must send men to bring {{gender:them|him}} back. They must hand {{gender:them|him}} over to the relative who avenges the death, and the murderer must die.

decisions.choice: the elders of his city: the town's leaders, who judged its cases
decisions.reason: The elders were the heads of families who led a town and settled its disputes at the gate (21:2-4, 19; 22:15). Here they act for the killer's home town, where the facts would be known.

decisions.choice: send and take him from there: bring the murderer out of the city of refuge
decisions.reason: The city of refuge gives no protection to a murderer. Even the LORD's altar did not protect one who killed on purpose (Exodus 21:14; Numbers 35:21).

decisions.choice: give him into the hand of the avenger: the relative carries out the sentence
decisions.reason: Once the elders have found the killing to be murder, the avenger puts the murderer to death, as Numbers 35:19, 21 also says.

decisions.choice: murderer
decisions.reason: This verse follows the case of a deliberate killing, so Balanced and Readable say "murderer", as in Numbers 35:16-21. Literal keeps "his" and "him".

decisions.choice: send men
decisions.reason: "Send" has no object in the Hebrew. Readable says who is sent: men to bring the murderer back.

source.text: לֹא־תָח֥וֹס עֵֽינְךָ֖ עָלָ֑יו וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֧ דַֽם־הַנָּקִ֛י מִיִּשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְט֥וֹב לָֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not will pity your eye on him, and you will remove [the] blood of the innocent from Israel, and [it will be] good for you.

en.L: Your eye shall not pity him; and you shall remove the blood of the innocent from Israel, and it will be good for you.
en.B: Show {{gender:them|him}} no pity. You must remove from Israel the guilt of innocent blood, so that it may go well with you.
en.R: Do not feel sorry for {{gender:them|him}}. You must clear Israel of the guilt for killing an innocent person. Then things will go well for you.

decisions.choice: your eye shall not pity: show no pity
decisions.reason: The eye stands for the feeling that looks on someone with pity. The same words are used in 7:16, 13:9 and verse 21.

decisions.choice: remove the blood of the innocent: clear away the guilt of a murder
decisions.reason: When an innocent person is murdered, the guilt lies on the land and the people until the murderer is punished (21:9; Numbers 35:33). The verb is the one in the refrain "remove the evil from your midst" (17:7; verse 19).

decisions.choice: and it will be good for you: it will go well with you
decisions.reason: The clause gives the result of obeying, as in 6:18 and 12:28.

decisions.choice: the guilt of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "guilt", since what is removed is not blood itself but the guilt it brings. Literal keeps "the blood".

source.text: לֹ֤א תַסִּיג֙ גְּב֣וּל רֵֽעֲךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּבְל֖וּ רִאשֹׁנִ֑ים בְּנַחֲלָֽתְךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּנְחַ֔ל בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לְךָ֖ לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not you will move [the] boundary of your neighbor which set [the] former [ones] in your inheritance which you will inherit in the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you to possess it.

en.L: You shall not move your neighbor's boundary, which the former ones set, in your inheritance that you will inherit in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to take possession of [it].
en.B: Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you will receive in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you as your own.
en.R: Do not move the stone that marks the edge of your neighbor's land. The people who came before you put it there to mark the share you will receive in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you to own.

decisions.choice: boundary: here the marker that shows where a field ends
decisions.reason: The word means a border, and here the stone or post that marks it. Moving it took part of a neighbor's land (27:17; Proverbs 22:28).

decisions.choice: your inheritance: the family's share of the land
decisions.reason: Each family's land was its lasting inheritance from the LORD and was not to pass out of it (Numbers 36:7; 1 Kings 21:3). Moving a boundary was theft of that inheritance, and Hosea 5:10 uses it as a picture of grave wrong.

decisions.choice: the former ones: those who came before
decisions.reason: From where Moses stands, the land has not yet been divided. The law looks ahead to a time when the markers set at the first division (Joshua 14-19) have stood for generations.

decisions.choice: boundary marker / the stone that marks the edge
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the marker, which is what can be moved. Literal keeps "boundary".

source.text: לֹֽא־יָקוּם֩ עֵ֨ד אֶחָ֜ד בְּאִ֗ישׁ לְכָל־עָוֺן֙ וּלְכָל־חַטָּ֔את בְּכָל־חֵ֖טְא אֲשֶׁ֣ר יֶֽחֱטָ֑א עַל־פִּ֣י׀שְׁנֵ֣י עֵדִ֗ים א֛וֹ עַל־פִּ֥י שְׁלֹשָֽׁה־עֵדִ֖ים יָק֥וּם דָּבָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will stand witness one against a man for any iniquity and for any sin, in any sin which he will sin; on [the] mouth of two witnesses or on [the] mouth of three witnesses will stand a matter.

en.L: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or for any sin, in any sin that he commits; on the word of two witnesses or on the word of three witnesses a matter shall stand.
en.B: One witness alone is not enough to convict anyone of any crime or wrong, whatever the offense may be. A case can stand only on the evidence of two or three witnesses.
en.R: One witness is never enough to prove that someone has done wrong, no matter what the wrong is. There must be two or three witnesses before a case can be decided.

decisions.choice: shall not stand ... shall stand: be enough to decide, be established
decisions.reason: The same verb opens and closes the verse. One witness's word does not stand, that is, it does not settle a case; a matter stands, is established, on the word of two or three.

decisions.choice: iniquity, sin, sin: any wrongdoing at all
decisions.reason: Three words for wrongdoing are piled up to cover every kind of charge. The rule of 17:6 and Numbers 35:30 for cases of death applies to every case.

decisions.choice: on the mouth of: on the testimony of
decisions.reason: As in 17:6, "mouth" stands for what witnesses say.

decisions.choice: two or three witnesses: a rule taken up in the New Testament
decisions.reason: Jesus and Paul apply this rule (Matthew 18:16; 2 Corinthians 13:1; 1 Timothy 5:19).

decisions.choice: is not enough to convict ... A case can stand only
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what it means for a witness to "stand" against someone: to win the case against them. Literal keeps the repeated verb.

source.text: כִּֽי־יָק֥וּם עֵד־חָמָ֖ס בְּאִ֑ישׁ לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּ֖וֹ סָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If rises a witness of violence against a man to testify against him [of] turning aside,

en.L: If a witness of violence rises up against a man to testify against him [of] turning aside,
en.B: If a witness who means harm comes forward to accuse someone of wrongdoing,
en.R: Suppose a witness who wants to hurt someone stands up and says that person has done wrong.

decisions.choice: a witness of violence: a witness whose testimony is meant to harm
decisions.reason: The word means violence or wrong done to others. A "witness of violence" uses the court to injure someone (Exodus 23:1; Psalm 35:11).

decisions.choice: turning aside: wrongdoing, perhaps turning away from the LORD
decisions.reason: The word means a turning aside. In 13:6 it is used of urging people to turn away from the LORD, and it may mean that charge here. Here it may also mean any departure from the law, which fits the general rule of verse 15.

decisions.choice: a witness rises: one accuser
decisions.reason: After verse 15, the case is that of a single accuser. The court of verse 17 must find out whether the charge is true.

decisions.choice: wrongdoing / done wrong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the general sense; the narrower sense is in the decision above.

source.text: וְעָמְד֧וּ שְׁנֵֽי־הָאֲנָשִׁ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־לָהֶ֥ם הָרִ֖יב לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לִפְנֵ֤י הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ וְהַשֹּׁ֣פְטִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְי֖וּ בַּיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: then will stand the two the men who [belong] to them the dispute before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges who will be in the days those.

en.L: then the two men who have the dispute shall stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, before the priests and the judges who will be in those days.
en.B: then the two people who have the dispute must stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of the priests and the judges in office at that time.
en.R: Then both people in the dispute must stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, in front of the priests and the judges who are serving at that time.

decisions.choice: before the LORD: at the place of worship, before the court there
decisions.reason: To stand before the LORD is to come to the place he chooses (17:8). There the priests and judges hear the case on his behalf (1:17; 17:9-12).

decisions.choice: the two men who have the dispute: the accuser and the accused
decisions.reason: Both sides must appear. The law speaks of men, as its cases usually do, but it covers anyone who brings or faces a charge.

decisions.choice: who will be in those days: whoever holds office at the time
decisions.reason: As in 17:9, Moses speaks of the future, when priests and judges will follow one another in office.

decisions.choice: people; in office / serving at that time
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use inclusive words for the two sides, and say "in office" or "serving" for "who will be in those days", as in 17:9.

source.text: וְדָרְשׁ֥וּ הַשֹּׁפְטִ֖ים הֵיטֵ֑ב וְהִנֵּ֤ה עֵֽד־שֶׁ֨קֶר֙ הָעֵ֔ד שֶׁ֖קֶר עָנָ֥ה בְאָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And will investigate the judges thoroughly, and behold, a witness of falsehood the witness; falsehood he testified against his brother,

en.L: And the judges shall investigate thoroughly; and indeed, the witness [is] a false witness; he has testified falsely against his brother,
en.B: The judges are to look into the matter carefully. If the witness proves to be a liar who has given false evidence against a fellow Israelite,
en.R: The judges must check the facts carefully. They may find that the witness has lied about another Israelite.

decisions.choice: investigate thoroughly: search out the facts with care
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or inquire, and the added word means "well". The judges must make a careful search, as in 13:15 and 17:4.

decisions.choice: and indeed: what the inquiry finds
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to what the judges discover. Here it introduces one possible outcome: that the witness lied.

decisions.choice: his brother: a fellow Israelite
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy's laws "brother" means any member of the people of Israel (15:2-3, 7).

decisions.choice: indeed / If / They may find
decisions.reason: Literal says "indeed" for the attention word, avoiding the old "behold". Balanced makes it a condition; Readable a possible finding.

source.text: וַעֲשִׂ֣יתֶם ל֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר זָמַ֖ם לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לְאָחִ֑יו וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: then you will do to him just as he planned to do to his brother, and you will remove the evil from your midst.

en.L: then you shall do to him as he planned to do to his brother. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.
en.B: do to that witness what the witness intended to do to the other person. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.
en.R: If so, do to the witness what the witness wanted to happen to the other person. This is how you must get rid of the evil among you.

decisions.choice: planned: plotted harm
decisions.reason: The verb means to devise or plot. The false witness is punished for what he set out to do, whether or not it came about.

decisions.choice: do to him as he planned: the penalty matches the harm intended
decisions.reason: The false witness receives the sentence the accused would have received. If the charge carried death, the liar dies; this protects the court from being used to do wrong (verse 21).

decisions.choice: remove the evil from your midst: get rid of the evil completely
decisions.reason: The refrain of Deuteronomy's laws, as in 13:6 and 17:7.

decisions.choice: you all, then you: from plural to singular
decisions.reason: "You shall do" speaks to the people as a group, "you shall remove" to the nation as one. Deuteronomy often moves between the two with no change in meaning (13:1).

decisions.choice: that witness ... the other person
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the witness and the one accused instead of using "him" and "his brother", so that it is clear who is who.

source.text: וְהַנִּשְׁאָרִ֖ים יִשְׁמְע֣וּ וְיִרָ֑אוּ וְלֹֽא־יֹסִ֨פוּ לַעֲשׂ֜וֹת ע֗וֹד כַּדָּבָ֥ר הָרָ֛ע הַזֶּ֖ה בְּקִרְבֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the remaining [ones] will hear and fear, and not they will add to do again like the thing the evil this in your midst.

en.L: And those who remain shall hear and fear, and they shall not again do anything like this evil thing in your midst.
en.B: Everyone else will hear of it and be afraid, and none of them will ever again do anything so evil among you.
en.R: Everyone else will hear what happened and be afraid. Then no one will ever do such an evil thing among you again.

decisions.choice: those who remain: everyone else in Israel
decisions.reason: The word means those who are left. Here it is the rest of the people, who learn from the punishment of the false witness.

decisions.choice: hear and fear: the punishment is a public warning
decisions.reason: The same words close the laws in 13:12, 17:13 and 21:21. Justice done in the open teaches the whole people.

decisions.choice: ever again
decisions.reason: "They will not add to do again" means they will not do it any more. Balanced and Readable say "ever again".

source.text: וְלֹ֥א תָח֖וֹס עֵינֶ֑ךָ נֶ֣פֶשׁ בְּנֶ֗פֶשׁ עַ֤יִן בְּעַ֨יִן֙ שֵׁ֣ן בְּשֵׁ֔ן יָ֥ד בְּיָ֖ד רֶ֥גֶל בְּרָֽגֶל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And not will pity your eye: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

en.L: And your eye shall not pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
en.B: Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
en.R: Do not feel sorry for the false witness. The punishment must match the harm: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth, a hand for a hand, a foot for a foot.

decisions.choice: your eye shall not pity: show no pity
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: life for life ... foot for foot: the penalty equal to the harm
decisions.reason: This is the rule of equal penalty given in Exodus 21:23-25 and Leviticus 24:19-20. Here it is applied to the false witness, who must suffer what he tried to bring on another. It is a rule for the judges, and it also sets a limit: the penalty may be no greater than the wrong.

decisions.choice: eye for eye, tooth for tooth: quoted by Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus quotes these words in Matthew 5:38-39, where he teaches his followers not to take revenge for personal wrongs.

decisions.choice: for the false witness; The punishment must match the harm
decisions.reason: Readable says who is not to be pitied, from verses 18-19, and states the rule before the list so that its point is clear.
